title: The linearized adjunction $P_{\mathcal B}\dashv G_{\mathcal B}$
statement:
In the situation of [def-sfb-modobj-linearization-right-adjoint], the adjunction
bijection of $P\dashv G$ restricts to a bijection between $\mathcal B$-linear maps
$PM\to N$ and $S\mathcal B$-linear maps $M\to GN$. This gives an adjunction
$$
P_{\mathcal B}\dashv G_{\mathcal B}\colon\Mod_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal D)\to\Mod_{S\mathcal B}(\mathcal C)
$$
between the linearizations of [def-sfb-modobj-linearization] and
[def-sfb-modobj-linearization-right-adjoint].

proof.text:
Let $M$ be an $S\mathcal B$-module and $N$ a $\mathcal B$-module, with actions $\gamma_M$ and $\gamma_N$. By [def-sfb-modobj-linearization], the action on $P_{\mathcal B}M$ is $a_M=P\gamma_M\circ\pi_{\mathcal B,M}^{-1}$. By the module-morphism equation of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], a map $\varphi:PM\to N$ is $\mathcal B$-linear if and only if $\varphi\circ a_M=\gamma_N\circ(\mathcal B\otimes\varphi)$. Precomposing both sides with the isomorphism $\pi_{\mathcal B,M}$ gives the equivalent equation
$$\varphi\circ P\gamma_M=\gamma_N\circ(\mathcal B\otimes\varphi)\circ\pi_{\mathcal B,M}.$$

Use the adjunction $P\dashv G$ with counit $c$ from [def-sfb-modobj-linearization-right-adjoint]. Write its unit as $u$ and its hom-bijection as $H_{X,Y}:\operatorname{Hom}(PX,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(X,GY)$. Explicitly $H(a)=G(a)\circ u_X$ and $H^{-1}(b)=c_Y\circ P(b)$. For $t:X'\to X$ and $v:Y\to Y'$, functoriality and naturality of $u$ give
$$H(v\circ a\circ P(t))=G(v)\circ G(a)\circ G(P(t))\circ u_{X'}=G(v)\circ H(a)\circ t.$$
For $\psi=H(\varphi)$, we therefore have $\varphi=c_N\circ P\psi$ and $H(\varphi\circ P\gamma_M)=\psi\circ\gamma_M$. These are substitutions into the hom-bijection of the assumed adjunction.

By naturality in the second variable of the projection formula [def-sfb-projection-formula], applied to $\psi:M\to GN$,
$$ (\mathcal B\otimes\varphi)\circ\pi_{\mathcal B,M}=(\mathcal B\otimes c_N)\circ(\mathcal B\otimes P\psi)\circ\pi_{\mathcal B,M}=(\mathcal B\otimes c_N)\circ\pi_{\mathcal B,GN}\circ P(S\mathcal B\otimes\psi). $$
By [def-sfb-modobj-linearization-right-adjoint], $\theta_{\mathcal B,N}=H((\mathcal B\otimes c_N)\circ\pi_{\mathcal B,GN})$. Apply the formula of step 2 to this composite, with precomposition $S\mathcal B\otimes\psi$ and postcomposition $\gamma_N$. The right side of the linearity equation in step 1 has adjoint
$$G(\gamma_N)\circ\theta_{\mathcal B,N}\circ(S\mathcal B\otimes\psi).$$
Since $H$ preserves and reflects equality, step 1 is equivalent to
$$\psi\circ\gamma_M=G(\gamma_N)\circ\theta_{\mathcal B,N}\circ(S\mathcal B\otimes\psi).$$

source.place: naturality of the projection formula and the two adjoints

proof.text: The composite $b_N=G(\gamma_N)\circ\theta_{\mathcal B,N}$ is exactly the action on $G_{\mathcal B}N$ in [def-sfb-modobj-linearization-right-adjoint]. Hence the last equation of step 3 is precisely the $S\mathcal B$-linearity equation for $\psi$ from [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Both directions hold because $H$ is a bijection. Define the module hom-bijection by $\varphi\mapsto H(\varphi)$, with inverse $\psi\mapsto H^{-1}(\psi)$; their inverse identities are those of $H$. For module maps $m:M'\to M$ and $n:N\to N'$, its naturality is the explicit formula $H(n\circ\varphi\circ Pm)=G(n)\circ H(\varphi)\circ m$ of step 2. These are the underlying maps of the linearized functors [def-sfb-modobj-linearization] and [def-sfb-modobj-linearization-right-adjoint], so these natural hom-bijections define the claimed adjunction $P_{\mathcal B}\dashv G_{\mathcal B}$.
